reason: This draft gets the main call right. Marisol asked whether she can keep running 53 miles, and it tells her plainly and honestly that she can't. It explains that the jump was too big: going from 27 to 37 to 53 miles means a rise of about 40% two weeks in a row. Next week adds up to about 39 miles (6+8+5+4+16). That pulls back to her planned level, close to the 37 miles of the week before, which is a sensible next step for her build. It also keeps her usual pattern: rest on Monday and Friday, the session on Wednesday and the long run on Sunday. Each day is clear enough to run as written. Her calves are only tight, not painful, and the draft does flag them, so running the 4 miles at marathon pace on Wednesday doesn't break the rule against quality work through pain. I marked it down for three reasons. First, it says she ran a 20-mile long run, which the card never mentions. Second, it starts the mileage at "about 30", which blurs the numbers. Third, the calf flag says only "watch the calves" and doesn't tell her what to do if the tightness turns into pain, such as dropping the Wednesday session or seeing a professional.
